notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

PC games run much faster when they look for NVIDIA's driver library: they now see an AMD GPU. Proton tells games the GPU is NVIDIA, but the library NVIDIA games use cannot run here, and some games kept trying to load it. Stray did it about 350 times a second; its menu went from about 10 frames a second to between 20 and 25. If a game will not start with this, set it back in its Performance menu: GPU shown to the game, NVIDIA.

PC games over USB: the console's USB drive on your PC has a PC Games folder. Copy a game's whole folder into it and it becomes a PC game, kept on the console's storage with no 4 GB limit. When the console cannot tell which program starts it, pick that on the web page's PC Games tab.

DOS games: a new DOS tab, played through DOSBox Pure. Add a game as a zip of its folder, or a .dosz, and it is kept whole. A zip with only a program inside goes to Unsorted, where you can pick DOS. DOSBox Pure's own start menu lists the programs a game has, and L3 opens its menu with an on-screen keyboard and a controller mapper. MIDI music is silent for now; Sound Blaster and AdLib music play.

A game's first launch uses the best settings reported for your console type in the Compatibility view, when there are some and you have not set any yourself. The launch screen says so, and you can change them any time.

TV picture size, in Settings, Display and Sound, Screen: for a TV that cuts off the edges of the picture, lower it until the edges of the menus show. Games get the same smaller picture. RetroArch games draw it themselves and keep every frame. Other games go through the console's compositor for it, as with Tear-free display, so the Jak games and Halo, which normally skip it, show about four frames in five while it is below 100%. Your TV's own Just Scan or Screen Fit setting, if it has one, does the same with no cost.

Rumble that kept going until another rumble now stops when the game stops it. The cause was a stop the system could drop; the console now sends a quiet kick after the last rumble, which leaves a long rumble alone.

Ports and Apps have Set hotkeys again, leaving out what cannot run there, like fast-forward and rewind. Gen1Recomp, Wind Waker HD and Black Ops Zombies can be remapped, button by button.

Deep sleep: the warning that the last deep sleep did not come back clears after a deep sleep that comes back on its own.

CPU Settings: the measured voltage for the top clock read low, because samples taken while the CPU was idle counted. It now follows what the chip really draws there.

New and lightly tested: the AMD GPU change was tried with Stray only. TV picture size has not been tried on a TV yet. DOS button presses in a game are not checked yet. The rumble fix was checked with the console's own Joy-Cons, not yet with a Pro Controller, and the deep sleep warning fix has not run on a console yet.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
